ShinyApp Options Data Management

Source: vignettes/ShinyApp_3A_Options_Data.Rmd
ShinyApp_3A_Options_Data.Rmd

Options Data Issues and Overview

As of 2026, Alphavantage has some pre-canned option metrics, but none that are relevant to valuation. They do, however, have full histories of option-level data which (once downloaded) can be used for almost any analysis desired.

Unlike simple time series data, options data requires knowing three more dimensions per point in time, per ticker. Specifically, a complete set of options requires a schema with 5 keys: Symbol, timestamp, expiration, strike, and put vs call. Needless to say, that’s more data than could ever be retrieved in real time. It’s also more data than comfortably fits inside any one given data.table. The only option then is to download (and process) the data outside of the Shiny app.

This vignette describes the procedure for downloading options data and how it is summarized for external use. In particular, the underlying data can be used to construct

  • Constant maturity implied volatilities at a number of deltas using the SSVI volatility surface interpolation method Gatheral and Jacquier for a given symbol and date.
  • Closest option to a given delta moneyness (e.g. 25 delta call or -25 delta put) for a given symbol and date.

The data from these efforts can be used externally using av_load_shinydata() or via user-developed functions as could be added using av_add_analytic()

Adding Full Option sets

The function av_add_options() handles all options downloads. Given a set of tickers and a date range (specified in the usual way, e.g. "-1y::"), it will use the HISTORICAL_OPTIONS API call to get a full set of options per symbol and date. If no symbols are specified, it will either start the database out with SPY or download all tickers that have previously been requested.

For example, to download all data for the (currently hot) ticker MU for the past year, just run:

> av_add_options("update",dtstr="-1y::",symbols=c("MU"))
Option data to get:MU from 2025-11-06 to 2026-11-06 (252 days)
AVOpt:MU (2025-11-06::2026-11-06) [=============] 100% [ 4m]
 Now: 16:34:16 Estimated end time data collection from AV: 16:38:13
Option update: Adding 1937969 rows to partitioned parquet set

Returned 1937969 new options, refreshing inventory, took 2.97 secs
Updated option inventory in 0.36sec
NULL
>

Note that downloading options data can take a considerable amount of time depending on what level of service you are paying for and the speed of your underlying infrastructure. With a simple limit of 70 requests per minute, the above operation took about 4 minutes. Collecting data for index ETFs in particular takes longer simply due to the volume of data requested. Initial data population may take several hours if not days, but once done, updates are fairly fast.

A note on storage

The av_add_options() call downloads all data, which can be substantial given the number of independent dimensions as outlined above. Alphavantage provides full greeks as well as last trades, marks, bid/offers and market sizes and volumes per contract id (i.e. per option with given expiration and strike for a given symbol).

This data is certainly too large to keep in one file (or data.frame()), so this package instead stores the data as a partitioned parquet directory below the user specified cache directory. For example, the data downloaded above was stored underneath my cache directory c:\t\avsh as

Directory of C:\t\avsh\eqopt\symbol=MU

11/07/2026  16:34    <DIR>          .
11/07/2026  16:34    <DIR>          ..
11/07/2026  16:34       104,243,776 part-0.parquet

As this data is stored in a different format, it requires the function av_load_cached_opts() to retrieve individual records. For example, to retrieve first and second month calls for the tickers JPM and GS over the past year, just run (for example)

> opttest2=av_load_cached_opts(optsDT=CJ(symbol=c("JPM","GS"), expcode=c("MO_1","MO_2"), type=c("call")), dtstr="-1y::")
> opttest2

Summarizing the data.

The raw options data needs to be aggregated in some way to be truly useful. There are two different techniques coded into this package. Each tries to find an option or option volatility that are closest to a given delta category for a given expiration, date, and symbol. There are three methods of aggregation available:

Simple inventory of data available.

The inventory option creates an internal list of three data.tables: An inventory summary, a table of symbols and dates for which options have been downloaded, and the last dates’ data for each ticker. Note that this process can a minute or two.

> av_add_options("inventory",dtstr="-1m::")
Updated option inventory in 26.72sec
NULL

Using the data is as simple as the following:

> head(av_load_shinydata("eqoptinv")$inv)
 symbol min_DT_ENTRY max_DT_ENTRY   cnt  nYrs nperYr min_ivn_dt max_ivn_dt min_iv_dt max_iv_dt

    AMD   2018-11-02   2026-11-06   444  8.02   55.4       <NA>       <NA>      <NA>      <NA>
   ARGT   2021-04-09   2026-11-06   312  5.58   55.9       <NA>       <NA>      <NA>      <NA>

Closest Option:

Find the option for a given expiration tenor which is closest (e.g.) to a 25 delta call, by date and symbol. Culling them from the database is accomplished with the "iv_nearest" option

> av_add_options("iv_nearest",dtstr="-2w::")
restore_avs_state restoring lazy loaded datasets iv_nearest
AV IV NEAR  [=================================>-]  98% [14s] save_avs_state(all|px|fst) writing iv_nearest,
NULL
>

To retrieve this data, use

Constant maturity Fair Value vols

This calculates fair value (arbitrage free) implied volatilities for a given delta moneyness and fixed tenor, using the SSVI approach of Gatheral and Jacquier The fair value fits are created using the "iv_fv" function, which will create/update a internal table iv with

  • Fair value volatilities for each fixed maturity expiration, e.g. for next monthly expiration 25 delta calls on SPY for a given date.
  • Fair value volatilities for a constant maturity date (defined as CWK_1 or CMO_1 for 1 week and 1 month out (e.g.) resepctively. There are three tenors for each, so the full set of expiration codes calculated are in (CWK_1,CWK_2,CWK_3,CMO_1,CMO_2,CMO_3).
> av_add_options("iv_fv",dtstr="-2w::")
restore_avs_state restoring lazy loaded datasets iv
Updating SOFR levels from FRED via quantmod
 save_avs_state(all|px|fst) writing pxd,
av_one_px(SOFR  @ userdata) userdata
...
 save_avs_state(all|px|fst) writing iv,
NULL
>

Note that SOFR rates are used as risk free rates for purposes of calculating forwards prices. The data calculated can be retrieved using (e.g.):

> av_load_shinydata("iv")[symbol=="QQQ" & ts==max(ts),]
         ts expcode moneyn strike    iv symbol
     <Date>  <char> <fctr>  <num> <num> <char>

 2026-11-06   CMO_1    P50    665 0.297    QQQ
 2026-11-06   CMO_1    P25    660 0.293    QQQ
